description: What decision: decompress_gunbatch uses decoder.take(limit + 1) before read_to_end, then checks out.len() > limit. Why right: enforces the decompressed-size cap without ever allocating more than limit+1 bytes. A naive approach (decompress fully then check) would materialise a multi-GiB allocation from a tiny gzip bomb before rejecting it — a memory DoS. The take() pattern turns an allocation bomb into a bounded read that stops at limit+1 bytes. Alternatives rejected: (1) custom Read wrapper tracking bytes — more code for same effect; (2) chunked read loop with manual accounting — correct but more complex; (3) check compressed-to-decompressed ratio heuristic — unreliable because ratio is data-dependent.
title: DECISION: .take(limit+1) streaming cap for gzip bomb defense
